themes_detail.label: Helicopter Noise Surge
themes_detail.summary: Helicopter noise complaints spiked to 76 this week, a 264% increase from the 8-week baseline average of 20.9 weekly complaints, suggesting a sudden operational change or event driving aerial traffic over Murray Hill/Gramercy.
evidence: 76 helicopter noise complaints this week vs. 20.9 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (264% spike, z-score: 8.6)
Helicopter noise is the 7th leading complaint type overall (348 complaints over 90 days), now accelerating sharply
This week's spike is the most recent statistically significant anomaly in the dataset
reporting_angles: Investigate what triggered the surge: new flight path, special events, military/NYPD operations, or private aviation patterns
Interview residents about sleep disruption and quality-of-life impact; check if other neighborhoods are experiencing similar spikes

themes_detail.label: Non-Emergency Police Calls Spike
themes_detail.summary: Non-Emergency Police Matter complaints jumped to 4 this week, tripling the 8-week baseline average of 1.0 complaint per week, indicating a potential emerging public safety or nuisance behavior concern.
evidence: 4 non-emergency police complaints this week vs. 1.0 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (300% spike, z-score: 3.46)
This is the newest spike in the dataset (reported THIS WEEK)
Suggests a pattern just beginning to emerge, not yet visible to community boards or local news
reporting_angles: Obtain NYPD incident logs for CD 106 this week to identify what specific behaviors or incidents drove calls
Canvass residents and block associations to identify emerging quality-of-life issues (street harassment, aggressive panhandling, etc.)

themes_detail.label: Street Signs Going Missing
themes_detail.summary: Missing street sign complaints spiked to 9 two weeks ago, a 1700% increase from the 8-week baseline of 0.5 complaints per week, pointing to possible systematic removal, theft, or infrastructure breakdown in the district.
evidence: 9 street sign complaints two weeks ago vs. 0.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (1700% spike, z-score: 12.02)
Highest z-score anomaly in the dataset, indicating strongest statistical deviation from baseline
No follow-up spike reported last week, suggesting either issue was resolved or complaints dropped
reporting_angles: Check DOT maintenance records: Are street signs being replaced, or have they gone missing due to theft/vandalism?
Photograph and map where signs are missing to identify geographic hotspots; interview DOT about cause and remediation timeline

themes_detail.label: Cannabis Retailer Complaints Cluster
themes_detail.summary: Cannabis retailer complaints jumped to 3 two weeks ago, a 2300% spike from the 8-week baseline of 0.1 complaints per week, potentially signaling illegal retail operations or consumer disputes in a newly regulated market.
evidence: 3 cannabis retailer complaints two weeks ago vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (2300% spike, z-score: 8.69)
Second-highest z-score anomaly; suggests a sudden cluster event rather than long-term trend
Murray Hill/Gramercy has seen significant new cannabis retail licensing in 2023–2024
reporting_angles: Investigate which retailers generated complaints: Are they licensed? Check Office of Cannabis Management (OCM) database for compliance issues
Interview residents and business neighbors about specific complaints (odor, loitering, operating hours violations, unlicensed storefronts)

themes_detail.label: Park Rule Violations Surge
themes_detail.summary: Park rule violation complaints spiked to 4 last week, a 1500% increase from the 8-week baseline of 0.2 complaints per week, indicating a sudden pattern of rule-breaking in district parks (likely related to encampments, vendor activity, or seasonal behavior).
evidence: 4 park rule violation complaints last week vs. 0.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (1500% spike, z-score: 8.66)
Third-highest z-score anomaly; statistically significant departure from baseline
Encampment complaints are the 3rd leading complaint type district-wide (856 over 90 days), suggesting possible overlap
reporting_angles: Identify which parks are affected (likely Gramercy Park, Madison Square Park, or Stuyvesant Square); visit to observe violations firsthand
Interview Parks Department and park conservancies about what rule violations are being reported and enforcement response
